newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Lehman recommends Taiwan's First Int'l.
newsitem.headline: Lehman recommends Taiwan's First Int'l.

text.p: Lehman Brothers, the global investment bank, said on Tuesday it had initiated coverage on Taiwan's First International Computer Inc with a "1-buy" rating.

Lehman said in a statement that computer maker First International was significantly undervalued, with shares trading at a 30 percent discount to the market, and a 12 to 27 percent discount to the company's long-term growth rate.
"We estimate First International's earning per share will grow by 21 percent in 1997 and 38 percent in 1998," said Richard Wei, Lehman's technology analyst, in the statement.
The growth is driven by top-line growth as well as expanding margins derived from a better product mix, Wei said.
"We estimate First International's net income in 1997 will climb by 29 percent to T$1.975 billion, with earnings per share rising 21 percent to T$3.4," he said.
Lehman said First International's notebook computer and integrated circuits assembly and test businesses, all of which offer better margins, would continue to expand.
In 1996, First International's gross margin expanded to 10.5 percent from 9.9 percent, it said.
